sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Read each phrase aloud, then add the noun it describes. Notice how much information sits before the noun.
items: die bis Freitag zu erledigenden Aufgaben
sections.lede: Two minutes of reading trains your eye to find the noun at the end of a long phrase.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: By the end of this lesson you will be able to do these things.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: German can compress a whole relative clause into a phrase that sits before a noun. This is the style of reports, laws and academic texts.

blocks.text: A relative clause such as die Kosten, die steigen can become die steigenden Kosten. The verb turns into a participle, takes an adjective ending and moves in front of the noun. The result is shorter, denser and more formal.
Die seit Jahren steigenden Kosten belasten das Unternehmen.
blocks.en: The costs, which have been rising for years, are putting pressure on the company.

items: The present participle (Partizip I) ends in -end and describes something active or ongoing: steigend, zunehmend, wachsend.
The past participle (Partizip II) often describes a completed result or a passive relationship: geschrieben, betroffen, beschlossen.
Extended attributes can carry several words: die von der Kommission beschlossene Reform.
zu + present participle expresses an obligation: die zu erledigenden Aufgaben = the tasks that must be completed.

blocks.title: Find the noun first
blocks.text: When reading a long phrase, skip to the noun, then work backwards through the participle and its modifiers. German readers do this automatically; learners can train it.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: Two participles, one adjective ending, and a clear difference in meaning.

items: Partizip I is formed from the infinitive + d: steigen → steigend, zunehmen → zunehmend.
Before a noun, the participle takes the normal adjective ending: die steigenden Kosten, der geschriebene Text.
Extended attributes stand between the article and the noun: die [von der Kommission beschlossene] Reform.
The phrase must agree with the noun in gender, number and case: die betroffenen Personen, der betroffene Mann.
A relative clause is often clearer when the attribute becomes very long or when you are speaking rather than writing.

blocks.title: -end or ge-?
blocks.text: Ask whether the action is still happening or already complete. Steigende Kosten are still rising. Geschriebene Texte have already been written.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: These phrases are ready-made models. Learn the whole phrase, including the ending.

items.example: Die steigenden Kosten zwingen das Unternehmen zum Handeln.
items.exampleEn: The rising costs are forcing the company to act.

items.example: Der gestern geschriebene Text muss noch korrigiert werden.
items.exampleEn: The text written yesterday still needs to be corrected.

items.example: Die von der Reform betroffenen Personen erhalten Unterstützung.
items.exampleEn: The people affected by the reform receive support.

items.example: Die bis Freitag zu erledigenden Aufgaben sind im Anhang aufgeführt.
items.exampleEn: The tasks to be completed by Friday are listed in the appendix.

items.example: Die zunehmende Nachfrage nach Fachkräften ist deutlich.
items.exampleEn: The increasing demand for skilled workers is clear.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Each sentence contains one participial phrase. Identify the noun it describes.

items.de: Die steigenden Kosten zwingen das Unternehmen zum Handeln.
items.en: The rising costs are forcing the company to act.
items.note: steigenden is Partizip I: the costs are still rising.

items.de: Der gestern geschriebene Text muss noch korrigiert werden.
items.en: The text written yesterday still needs to be corrected.
items.note: geschriebene is Partizip II: the writing is complete.

items.de: Die von der Reform betroffenen Personen erhalten Unterstützung.
items.en: The people affected by the reform receive support.
items.note: The extended attribute is von der Reform betroffenen.

items.de: Die bis Freitag zu erledigenden Aufgaben sind im Anhang aufgeführt.
items.en: The tasks to be completed by Friday are listed in the appendix.
items.note: zu erledigenden expresses an obligation in the passive.

items.de: Die zunehmende Nachfrage nach Fachkräften ist deutlich.
items.en: The increasing demand for skilled workers is clear.
items.note: zunehmende is active: demand is increasing.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Participial phrases pack several unstressed endings together. Keep the stressed syllable strong.

items.hint: One syllable “shtai-gend”. The ei glides from a to i; the final -end is light.
Stress the second syllable: ge-SCHRIE-ben. The prefix ge- is short, the ie is long.
Stress the second syllable: be-TROf-fe-nen. Keep the o short and do not swallow the final -nen.
Stress the second syllable: er-LE-di-gen-den. Say each ending clearly; the word has five syllables.
Stress the second syllable: be-SCHLOS-se-ne. The sch is clean and the o is short.

sections.title: Cultural note
sections.heading: The elegant compressed sentence — and its limits

blocks.text: Participial attributes are a hallmark of German academic, legal and journalistic writing. They allow a writer to place a definition, a condition or a source directly before the noun, which keeps the main clause free for the argument.

The same structure can become a Schachtelsatz — a sentence nested inside itself. Newspapers and writing guides often advise splitting long attributes into relative clauses. In an exam, one well-built attribute shows control; three in one sentence usually cost clarity.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: An author and an editor decide where a participial phrase helps and where it does not.
sections.setting: An editor's office at a publishing house

lines.speaker: Redakteurin
lines.de: Dieser Satz ist zu lang: „Die von der Kommission nach langen Beratungen beschlossene und von vielen Kritikern abgelehnte Reform …“
lines.en: This sentence is too long: “The reform passed by the commission after long deliberations and rejected by many critics …”

lines.speaker: Autor
lines.de: Ich wollte die Informationen kompakt halten.
lines.en: I wanted to keep the information compact.

lines.speaker: Redakteurin
lines.de: Kompakt ja, aber der Leser verliert den Faden. Teilen Sie den Satz in zwei relative Sätze.
lines.en: Compact, yes, but the reader loses the thread. Split the sentence into two relative clauses.

lines.speaker: Autor
lines.de: Also: „Die Reform wurde nach langen Beratungen beschlossen. Viele Kritiker lehnen sie ab.“
lines.en: So: “The reform was passed after long deliberations. Many critics reject it.”

lines.speaker: Redakteurin
lines.de: Genau. Die kürzere Form „die beschlossene Reform“ reicht an anderer Stelle völlig aus.
lines.en: Exactly. The shorter form “the reform that was passed” is enough elsewhere.

lines.speaker: Autor
lines.de: Dann überarbeite ich den Absatz und behalte nur die wichtigen Partizipien.
lines.en: Then I will revise the paragraph and keep only the important participles.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Building an extended attribute
sections.lede: The noun comes last. Everything before it describes the noun.

rows: die Aufgaben, die erledigt werden müssen
die Reform, die die Kommission beschlossen hat
die von der Kommission beschlossene Reform
the reform passed by the commission

items: Start with the noun and its article: die Reform.
Add the agent or detail before the participle: von der Kommission.
Add the adjective ending that matches the noun: die von der Kommission beschlossene Reform.
For an obligation, use zu + Partizip I: die zu erledigenden Aufgaben.

blocks.title: Decoding strategy
blocks.text: Read the noun first, then ask “which one?”. In die seit Jahren steigenden Kosten, find Kosten, then steigenden, then seit Jahren. The phrase answers: which costs? The ones that have been rising for years.

sections.tip: If the phrase needs a comma to be understood, it probably needs a relative clause instead.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Check the difference between active -end forms and completed ge- forms.

options: the costs that have already risen
exercises.explanation: steigend is Partizip I and describes an ongoing, active process.

options: the text that is being written
the text that has been written
the text that must be written
exercises.explanation: geschrieben is Partizip II: the action is complete.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means “the tasks to be completed”?
exercises.explanation: zu + Partizip I expresses an obligation: die zu erledigenden Aufgaben.

exercises.prompt: Which extended attribute is correctly formed?
options: die von der Kommission beschlossene Reform
die von der Kommission beschlossen Reform
die beschlossene von der Kommission Reform
die Reform von der Kommission beschlossene
exercises.explanation: The attribute sits between article and noun, and the participle takes the adjective ending -e.

exercises.prompt: What is the Partizip I of zunehmen?

sections.title: Complete the sentence
sections.lede: Type the missing participle with the correct adjective ending.

exercises.prompt: Die ___ Kosten zwingen das Unternehmen zum Handeln.
exercises.explanation: steigen → steigend; plural nominative after die → steigenden.

exercises.prompt: Der gestern ___ Text muss noch korrigiert werden.
exercises.explanation: schreiben → geschrieben; masculine nominative after der → geschriebene.

exercises.prompt: Die von der Reform ___ Personen erhalten Unterstützung.
exercises.explanation: betreffen → betroffen; plural nominative after die → betroffenen.

exercises.prompt: Die bis Freitag ___ Aufgaben sind im Anhang aufgeführt.
exercises.explanation: zu + erledigend + plural ending: die zu erledigenden Aufgaben.

exercises.prompt: Die ___ Nachfrage nach Fachkräften ist deutlich.
exercises.explanation: zunehmen → zunehmend; feminine nominative after die → zunehmende.

sections.title: Build the sentence
sections.lede: Build each sentence. Keep the participial phrase directly before its noun.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The rising costs are forcing the company to act.”
exercises.answer: Die steigenden Kosten zwingen das Unternehmen zum Handeln.
exercises.explanation: Die steigenden Kosten is the subject; the participle sits before the noun.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The people affected by the reform receive support.”
exercises.answer: Die von der Reform betroffenen Personen erhalten Unterstützung.
exercises.explanation: The extended attribute von der Reform betroffenen stands between die and Personen.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The tasks to be completed by Friday are listed in the appendix.”
exercises.answer: Die bis Freitag zu erledigenden Aufgaben sind im Anhang aufgeführt.
exercises.explanation: bis Freitag modifies the obligation phrase zu erledigenden.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The text written yesterday still needs to be corrected.”
exercises.answer: Der gestern geschriebene Text muss noch korrigiert werden.
exercises.explanation: gestern modifies the participle geschriebene, which describes Text.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen twice. The speakers are discussing a formal text.
sections.speaker: An editor and an author

script.speaker: Redakteurin
script.de: Im ersten Absatz steht: „die von der Reform betroffenen Personen“. Das ist korrekt, aber schwer zu lesen.
script.en: The first paragraph says: “the people affected by the reform”. That is correct but hard to read.

script.speaker: Autor
script.de: Soll ich daraus einen Relativsatz machen?
script.en: Should I turn it into a relative clause?

script.speaker: Redakteurin
script.de: Ja. Schreiben Sie: „die Personen, die von der Reform betroffen sind“.
script.en: Yes. Write: “the people who are affected by the reform”.

script.speaker: Autor
script.de: Und was ist mit den steigenden Kosten im zweiten Absatz?
script.en: And what about the rising costs in the second paragraph?

script.speaker: Redakteurin
script.de: Die Form ist kurz und klar. Die kann bleiben.
script.en: That form is short and clear. It can stay.

questions.prompt: What does the editor want the author to change?
options: the extended attribute die von der Reform betroffenen Personen
the length of the second paragraph
questions.explanation: She says the phrase is correct but hard to read and suggests a relative clause.

questions.prompt: Why can die steigenden Kosten stay?
questions.explanation: The editor says: Die Form ist kurz und klar. Die kann bleiben.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Practise turning a relative clause into a phrase and back again.
sections.prompt: Describe a current development at work or in your studies. Use one present-participle phrase, one past-participle phrase and one zu + participle phrase.

model.de: In meinem Projekt gibt es drei wichtige Punkte: die steigende Nachfrage nach Beratung, die bereits beschlossenen Änderungen und die bis Monatsende zu erledigenden Aufgaben. Die steigende Nachfrage zeigt, dass wir unser Team erweitern müssen.
model.en: There are three important points in my project: the rising demand for advice, the changes that have already been decided, and the tasks to be completed by the end of the month. The rising demand shows that we need to expand our team.

tips: Say the noun first, then add the attribute: die Aufgaben — die zu erledigenden Aufgaben.
Keep the participle next to its noun; do not separate them with a long insert.
Afterwards, say the same idea as a relative clause to check that you understand it.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These errors usually come from translating the English word order word for word.

items.why: The participial attribute stands before the noun, not after it.

items.wrong: die von der Reform betroffen Personen
items.right: die von der Reform betroffenen Personen
items.why: The participle needs the adjective ending: plural nominative after die → -en.
The obligation pattern needs the participle form: zu + erledigend + ending.
Modifiers belong inside the attribute, before the participle and the noun.

questions.prompt: When is a relative clause usually the better choice?
options: When the phrase is only one word long
When the attribute becomes very long or the text is spoken
When the sentence is in the present tense
questions.explanation: Long or complex attributes are harder to process; a relative clause restores clarity.

questions.prompt: Die ___ Kosten zwingen das Unternehmen zum Handeln.
Der gestern ___ Text muss noch korrigiert werden.
Die von der Reform ___ Personen erhalten Unterstützung.

questions.prompt: Build: “The people affected by the reform receive support.”
